questions.question: Idealism is described as the oldest systematic philosophy in which cultural tradition?

options.C: Western Culture

options.C: At least as early as Socrates in ancient Egypt

questions.question: What do idealists generally believe to be the only true reality?

options.A: The material world perceived through the senses
options.B: Scientific laws and empirical observations
options.C: Ideas

questions.question: How do idealists characterize the material world?

options.B: As the foundation of all true knowledge
options.C: As characterized by change, instability, and uncertainty
options.D: As the highest form of reality

questions.explanation: The text states that idealists believe matter (the material world) is characterized by change, instability, and uncertainty.

questions.question: What is the idealist's position regarding the existence of the physical world?

options.A: The idealist completely denies the existence of the physical world
options.B: The idealist does not deny the existence of the physical world
options.C: The idealist believes the physical world is the only reality
options.D: The idealist is indifferent to questions about the physical world

questions.question: According to idealism, what is the status of physical things like houses, hills, and stars?

options.A: They are the ultimate and highest form of reality
options.B: They do not exist at all
options.C: They are real, but not ultimately real — they are manifestations of a more fundamental incorporeal reality

questions.question: What does idealism describe the physical world as being a manifestation of?

options.B: A more fundamental incorporeal reality
options.C: Mathematical laws and equations

questions.explanation: The text states that physical things are manifestations of a more fundamental incorporeal (non-physical) reality.

questions.question: How do idealists say we come to know the physical world around us?

options.B: Through religious revelation
options.C: Through our senses

questions.question: A modern idealist suggested that a more accurate name for the philosophy would be:

options.C: Idea-ism

questions.question: Why did a modern idealist suggest renaming idealism 'idea-ism'?

options.B: Because idealism is more concerned with ideas and concepts rather than the search for superfluous attainments
options.C: Because the word 'idealism' is too closely associated with politics

questions.question: According to the text, which three areas will be examined to understand idealism?

options.A: Platonic idealism, Aristotelian idealism, and modern idealism
options.B: Platonic idealism, religious idealism, and modern idealism
options.C: Platonic idealism, scientific idealism, and political idealism
options.D: Religious idealism, existential idealism, and modern idealism

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between philosophy and education according to the text?

questions.question: In the context of idealism, the term 'incorporeal' most nearly means:

options.C: Not composed of matter; non-physical

questions.question: Which statement would an idealist most likely agree with?

options.A: A rock is ultimately real because it can be seen and touched
options.B: A rock exists physically but is ultimately a manifestation of a deeper non-physical reality
options.C: A rock does not exist in any sense
options.D: A rock is real only because science can measure it

questions.explanation: Idealists do not deny the physical world but hold that physical things are not ultimately real — they are manifestations of a more fundamental incorporeal reality.

questions.question: What distinguishes idealism's focus from what the modern idealist called 'superfluous attainments'?

options.A: Idealism focuses on material wealth over spiritual pursuits
options.B: Idealism prioritizes ideas and concepts over superficial or unnecessary achievements
options.C: Idealism prioritizes physical science over abstract thought
options.D: Idealism is concerned with athletic and artistic achievement

questions.explanation: The text explains that idealism is more concerned with ideas and concepts rather than the search for superfluous (unnecessary/excessive) attainments, which is why 'idea-ism' was suggested as a better name.

questions.question: According to the text, understanding idealism is best achieved by:

options.B: Examining the works of outstanding philosophers connected with idealism
options.C: Studying political philosophy and government theory

questions.explanation: The text states that an adequate understanding of idealism will be better forged by examining the works of selected outstanding philosophers who were connected with idealism.

options.B: A new group of teachers who challenged old ideas in politics and ethics

questions.question: Plato's philosophy was largely a reaction to what condition?

options.A: The rigid and unchanging nature of Athenian society
options.B: The state of flux that greatly influenced Athenian culture
options.C: The dominance of military values over intellectual ones
options.D: The spread of Socratic ideas beyond Athens

questions.explanation: The passage states that Plato's philosophy, to a large extent, was a reaction to the state of flux that had greatly influenced Athenian culture.

questions.question: Which two works by Plato are mentioned in the passage?

options.B: The Phaedo and The Meno
options.C: The Republic and The Laws

questions.explanation: The passage explicitly mentions that two of Plato's famous works are the Republic and the Laws.

questions.question: In the Republic, what key distinction does Plato draw?

options.A: The separation of politics from ethics
options.B: The separation of the world of ideas from the world of matter
options.C: The separation of knowledge from belief
options.D: The separation of the state from the individual

questions.explanation: The passage states that in the Republic, Plato wrote about the separation of the world of ideas from the world of matter.

questions.question: According to Plato, what is the relationship between mind and matter?

options.A: Matter is basic or prior to mind
options.B: Mind and matter are equal and co-existing
options.C: Mind is basic or prior to matter
options.D: Both mind and matter are products of sensory experience

questions.explanation: The passage states that Plato emphasizes mind as being basic or prior to matter.

questions.question: What does Plato contend about the nature of mind and matter?

options.A: Mind is an illusion created by matter
options.B: Mind is real, while matter is a product of the mind
options.C: Matter is real, while mind is a product of matter
options.D: Both mind and matter are equally real

questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that Plato contends that mind is real, while matter is a product of the mind.

questions.question: According to Plato, what do people primarily concern themselves with?

options.B: The accumulation of material wealth
options.C: The search for truth

questions.explanation: The passage states that according to Plato, people concern themselves primarily with the search for truth.

questions.question: Why, according to Plato, can truth NOT be found in the world of matter?

options.A: Because the world of matter is governed by God alone
options.B: Because the world of matter is both imperfect and constantly changing
options.C: Because matter does not exist in any real sense
options.D: Because only sophists study the material world

questions.explanation: The passage explains that since truth is perfect and eternal, it cannot be found in the world of matter, which is both imperfect and constantly changing.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of truth, according to Plato's philosophy as described in the passage?

options.B: Sensory and observable
options.C: Perfect and eternal

questions.explanation: The passage states that truth is perfect and eternal, which is why it cannot be found in the imperfect, changing world of matter.

questions.question: According to Plato, what is the source of the world of ideas (or forms)?

options.B: Sensory experience and observation
options.C: God, the Source of all true knowledge

questions.explanation: The passage states that the world of ideas (or forms) has its source from God the Source of all true knowledge.

questions.question: Why does Plato argue that the ever-changing world of sensory data is not to be trusted?

options.A: Because sensory data is controlled by the sophists
options.B: Because sensory data belongs to the material world, which is imperfect and unreliable for finding eternal truth
options.C: Because the senses were destroyed during the Persian Wars
options.D: Because only God can interpret sensory data correctly

questions.question: What is dialectic, as referenced in Plato's philosophy?

options.A: A form of military strategy used by philosopher-kings
options.B: A method of critical discussion that moves from mere opinion to true knowledge
options.C: A curriculum focused on abstract mathematics
options.D: A political system governed by elected philosophers

questions.question: In Plato's dialectical method, thinking begins with what?

options.B: A mathematical proof
options.C: A thesis or point of view

questions.explanation: The passage states that in the dialectical process, thinking begins with a thesis or point of view.

options.A: The philosopher must abandon the discussion entirely
options.B: The philosopher must reexamine the former position
options.C: The philosopher must seek approval from the state
options.D: The philosopher must consult sensory evidence

questions.explanation: The passage states that when an opposite point of view (antithesis) is encouraged, a philosopher must reexamine the former position.

questions.question: According to Plato, do people create knowledge?

options.A: Yes, knowledge is created through sensory experience
options.B: Yes, knowledge is created through political debate
options.C: No, people discover knowledge rather than create it
options.D: No, only God creates knowledge and delivers it to rulers

questions.question: What did Plato conjecture about the human soul and knowledge?

options.A: The human soul has never possessed true knowledge
options.B: The human soul gains knowledge only through bodily experience
options.C: The human soul once had true knowledge but lost it when placed in a material body
options.D: The human soul creates new knowledge in each lifetime

questions.question: How does the material body affect the soul's knowledge, according to Plato?

options.A: It enhances and refines the soul's knowledge
options.B: It distorts and corrupts the knowledge the soul once had
options.C: It has no effect on the soul's capacity for knowledge
options.D: It transfers knowledge from the soul to the physical world

questions.explanation: The passage states that the material body distorted and corrupted the true knowledge that the human soul once possessed.

questions.question: What was the ultimate goal of the type of education Plato suggested?

questions.question: What was the educational path for those proficient in dialectic, according to Plato?

options.B: They would become military generals

questions.question: According to Plato, what dual role must the philosopher-king fulfill?

options.B: Be both a thinker and a doer
options.C: Be both a teacher of sophistry and a critic of it
options.D: Be both a sculptor of ideas and a writer of laws

questions.explanation: The passage states that Plato's idea was that the philosopher-king must not only be a thinker but a doer.

questions.question: What specific responsibilities did Plato assign to the philosopher-king?

options.B: To supervise the affairs of the state and teach others
options.C: To write laws and enforce them through military power

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Platonic Idealism's view of reality?

options.A: The material world is the only true reality
options.B: Sensory experience is the most reliable source of knowledge
options.C: The world of ideas is more real and reliable than the world of matter
options.D: Reality is defined by political power and social consensus

questions.question: The term 'world of forms' in Plato's philosophy refers to what?

options.A: The physical shapes and structures found in the natural world
options.B: The perfect, eternal world of ideas that is the source of true knowledge
options.C: The documented laws and political structures of the state
options.D: The artistic forms created by craftsmen in Athens

questions.question: How does Plato's educational philosophy reflect his broader metaphysical views?

options.A: By prioritizing military training as the path to the highest good
options.B: By grounding education in sensory observation and empirical data
options.C: By using abstract thinking and dialectic to guide bright minds toward true knowledge and the highest good
options.D: By rejecting the role of the state in shaping education

questions.question: Which ancient culture significantly influenced many New Testament writers?

options.C: Greek Culture

options.C: Judaism and Christianity

questions.question: When did Augustine live?

questions.question: Who was Plotinus?

options.A: A Roman emperor of the second century

options.D: A student of Alexander the Great

questions.question: Through what means did Plotinus believe people could return to the union source?

questions.question: What was Augustine's view regarding man and the sin of Adam?

options.B: Man inherited Adam's sin and is continuously struggling to regain his pre-fall innocence and purity
options.C: Man is not affected by Adam's sin if he seeks God

questions.question: Whose concept of the 'divided line' did Augustine build upon?

options.C: Plotinus

questions.question: In Augustine's philosophy, what does the World of God represent?

options.A: The material world of human civilization
options.B: The world of politics and governance
options.C: The World of Spirit and the Good

questions.question: In Augustine's philosophy, what characterizes the World of Man?

options.B: Material world of darkness, sin, ignorance, and suffering
options.C: A neutral space between God and nature
options.D: A place of physical pleasure and earthly joy

questions.question: What method of learning did Augustine strongly endorse, in agreement with Plato?

options.B: The Socratic questioning method
options.C: The dialectical method

questions.question: What approach to education did Augustine promote as a result of his belief in the dialectical method?

questions.question: What did Augustine and Plato both warn could lead people away from true knowledge?

options.C: Study of philosophy and logic

questions.question: According to Augustine, who creates knowledge?

options.B: Philosophers through dialectical thinking
options.C: God — people can only discover it

questions.question: How, according to Augustine, can people discover knowledge?

options.B: Through trying to find God

options.D: Through physical and moral discipline alone

questions.question: Why did Augustine believe humans are closest to Divinity among all things?

options.A: Because humans possess reason and language
options.B: Because humans have souls
options.C: Because humans were made in God's physical image
options.D: Because humans alone can perform worship

questions.question: Where did Augustine say humans should look for true knowledge?

options.B: In the natural world around them
options.C: Within their own souls
options.D: In the teachings of the Church

questions.explanation: Augustine said humans should look within their souls for the true knowledge that exists there, since the soul is closest to Divinity.

questions.question: What did Augustine consider to be ultimate reality?

options.B: The human mind
options.C: God

questions.explanation: Augustine believed that ultimate reality is God.

questions.question: According to Augustine, what is the human bridge to ultimate reality (God)?

options.B: Scripture
options.C: The Church

questions.explanation: Augustine believed that the human bridge to ultimate reality (God) is the soul.

questions.question: What did Plato consider to be ultimate reality, and what was the human bridge to it?

options.B: Idea; the mind
options.C: God; the soul

questions.explanation: According to the text, Plato's ultimate reality is idea, and the human bridge to it is the mind.

questions.question: What logical association does the text draw from comparing Augustine's and Plato's views on ultimate reality?

options.A: It is logical to associate the soul with matter
options.B: It is logical to associate God with idea
options.C: It is logical to associate the mind with God
options.D: It is logical to associate idea with darkness

questions.question: According to Augustine, what is man's means of contact with ultimate reality?

options.B: Scripture and prayer
options.C: Mind and soul

questions.explanation: The text states that man's contact with ultimate reality is by means of mind and soul.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Augustine's overall philosophical position?

questions.question: Which philosopher most directly influenced Augustine's educational and philosophical ideas?

options.B: Socrates
options.C: Plato

questions.question: How did Greek philosophy reach and influence Christianity, according to the text?

questions.question: What historical period informs the classification of 'Modern Idealism'?

options.B: The scientific revolution of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries
options.C: The Enlightenment of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries
options.D: The Industrial Revolution of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how Modern Idealism is characterized?

options.B: Rationalism and materialism
options.C: Systematization and subjectivism

questions.explanation: Modern Idealism is characterized by systematization and subjectivism, as gleaned in the writings of its notable writers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a notable writer associated with Modern Idealism?

options.B: George Berkeley
options.C: John Locke

questions.question: What were the years of Rene Descartes' life?
questions.explanation: Rene Descartes lived from 1596 to 1650.

questions.question: Although much of Descartes' philosophy is characterized as Idealism, what other philosophical system did he also contribute to?

options.B: Pragmatism
options.C: Philosophical realism

questions.question: Which of the following is one of Descartes' significant works?

options.B: Discourse on Method
options.C: Principles of Human Knowledge

questions.question: What is the major contribution of Descartes to Idealism?

options.B: The a priori judgment system
options.C: The Cartesian Principle

questions.explanation: The text states that the major contribution of Descartes to Idealism was his famous Cartesian Principle.

questions.question: What method did Descartes use when he sought to doubt all things, including his own existence?

options.B: Mathematical doubt
options.C: Empirical observation

questions.explanation: Descartes explored his 'mathematical doubt,' whereby he sought to doubt all things including his own existence.

questions.question: Upon which two principles did Descartes base his philosophical system?

options.B: Mind and Matter
options.C: The 'cogito' and Deity

questions.question: In Descartes' philosophy, what does the 'cogito' represent?

options.A: The foundation for all objects of thought
options.B: The indomitability of human thought
options.C: The existence of an omnipresent God
